back_content: The protection and wise management of natural resources like water. Example: Water conservation is essential to avoid severe shortages.
A state or situation in which something needed cannot be obtained in sufficient amounts. Example: The town faced a tap water shortage.
The collection and storage of rain for reuse on-site. Example: Rainwater harvesting collects roof runoff for garden use.
Traditional underground rainwater storage structures used in Rajasthan. Example: Desert homes store drinking water in clean Tankas.
Short and striking or memorable phrases used in advertising or campaigns. Example: Students held signs with water-saving slogans.
A large natural or artificial lake used as a source of water supply. Example: The city reservoir supplies water through pipes.
Of great value; not to be wasted or treated carelessly. Example: Water is a precious natural resource for all living beings.
A water storage tank placed high on a rooftop or structure. Example: The rooftop cement tank was shaped like a tractor.
A shortened form of a word or group of words with omitted letters replaced by an apostrophe. Example: 'Can't' is a contraction of 'cannot'.
Made according to individual specifications or artistic preferences. Example: In Punjab, water tanks are custom-built in fun shapes.
Scarcity, deficit, lack. Example: The water shortage caused hardship.
Abundance, surplus, plenty. Example: After rain, there was an abundance of water.
Valuable, priceless, treasured. Example: Clean water is a precious gift.
Worthless, cheap, disposable. Example: Never treat water as disposable.
Preservation, saving, protection. Example: Water conservation saves energy.
Waste, destruction, depletion. Example: Waste leads to severe water crises.
Motto, catchphrase, watchword. Example: 'Save Every Drop' is a catchy slogan.
Four syllables (/ˌkɒn.səˈveɪ.ʃən/). The 'tion' sounds like '/ʃən/'.
Silent letter 'l' in shouldn't (/ˈʃʊd.ənt/). The 'l' is completely silent.
Three syllables (/ˈrɛz.ə.vwɑːr/). The ending 'oir' sounds like '/vwɑːr/'.
Two syllables (/ˈprɛʃ.əs/). The 'ci' makes a '/ʃ/' sound.
Silent letter 't' in whistle (/ˈwɪs.əl/). The 't' is silent.
Cannot. Example: We can't waste a single drop of water.
Do not. Example: Don't leave the tap open while brushing teeth.
Should not. Example: We shouldn't pollute rivers and lakes.
Would not. Example: A responsible citizen wouldn't waste water.
Must not. Example: You mustn't waste drinking water.
To use water with extreme care and avoid any waste. Example: Students marched carrying signs that urged people to save every drop.
Losing or spending something very rapidly without holding on to it. Example: Money was slipping away like water through a sieve.
In trouble or difficulty. Example: Anyone who wastes water during a shortage will end up in hot water.
To stop the flow of water or resources. Example: Always turn off the tap after washing hands.
To be logical, valid, or reasonable. Example: Excuses for wasting water simply do not hold water.
